claims.text: A hybrid machine-learning potential periodically calibrated against sparse ab initio free-energy evaluations can substantially reduce the cost of calculating fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The hybrid framework can accurately capture key entropy contributions across solid and fluid phases.
The proposed framework can be extended from elemental and binary systems to selected multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning potential will be trained on a sparse set of ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots.
Periodic recalibration against ab initio data will correct the model for anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling.
Vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration effects are pronounced at approximately 0.9Tm to Tm.
The machine-learning potential acts as a surrogate for the ab initio potential-energy surface.
Periodic corrections maintain an accurate free-energy landscape and its associated entropy contributions.
Replacing full ab initio free-energy evaluation with the surrogate enables more efficient phase-space exploration.
Targeted ab initio corrections preserve the thermodynamic details required to determine fusion properties accurately.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 5 to 10 relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed method will predict free energies, melting temperatures, and latent heats within acceptable error margins relative to TOR-TILD.
Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD are accurate but computationally intensive, particularly for complex multicomponent systems.
The strategy is expected to be effective for elemental and binary systems near melting.
The strategy is expected to be effective for moderately complex high-entropy alloys.
Accuracy may degrade under extreme anharmonicity or outside the composition and temperature ranges represented in the training data.
Deviations greater than 5-10% in free-energy or entropy-derived observables, greater than 50-100 K in melting temperature, or a speedup below approximately fivefold would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated temperature interval of roughly 0.9Tm to Tm does not clearly include temperatures above Tm, yet the hypothesis and benchmark require sampling both solid and liquid phases across a range spanning the transition.
